claim: On 2026-08-04 Application and Network Load Balancers added TLS security policies that comply with RFC 9151 (CNSA 1.0 suite requirements).
question: When did Application and Network Load Balancers add RFC 9151 security policies, and is it examinable?

qualifiers.scope: Application Load Balancer HTTPS listeners and Network Load Balancer TLS listeners

evidence.quote: AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) and Network Load Balancer (NLB) now support new TLS-based security policies that comply with RFC 9151 TLS server requirements for Commercial National Security Algorithm (CNSA) 1.0 suite requirements.
Customers who are required to meet CNSA 1.0 TLS security requirements can now use ALB and NLB with RFC 9151 compliant security policies.

evidence.heading: AWS Application and Network Load Balancers now support RFC 9151 compliant security policies

note: d127. Not examinable yet (after the 2026-07-15 cutoff).

claim: On 2025-11-21 Application Load Balancers added health check logs, delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket every 5 minutes with no charge beyond S3 storage.
question: When did Application Load Balancers add health check logs, and what do they cost?

values.display: no additional charges beyond standard S3 storage costs

evidence.quote: AWS Application Load Balancers (ALB) now supports Health Check Logs that allows you to send detailed target health check log data directly to your designated Amazon S3 bucket.
Logs are automatically delivered to your S3 bucket every 5 minutes with no additional charges beyond standard S3 storage costs.

evidence.heading: AWS Application Load Balancer now supports Health Check Logs

claim: On 2025-11-20 Application Load Balancers launched Target Optimizer, which enforces a maximum number of concurrent requests on a target with an agent that runs on the targets; its traffic generates more LCU usage than regular target groups.
question: What is ALB Target Optimizer and how does it change the bill?

values.display: enforce a maximum number of concurrent requests

evidence.quote: Application Load Balancer (ALB) now offers Target Optimizer, a new feature that allows you to enforce a maximum number of concurrent requests on a target.
Once enabled, the feature works with the help of an agent provided by AWS that you run on your targets that tracks request concurrency.
Traffic to target groups that enable Target Optimizer generates more LCU usage than regular target groups.

evidence.heading: AWS Application Load Balancer launches Target Optimizer

note: d132. Current truth: elb-alb-target-optimizer-no-sticky-more-lcu. The FAQ gives the Target Optimizer LCU sizes (numbers lens).

claim: On 2026-07-23 Amazon CloudWatch Logs added Application Load Balancer access, connection and health check logs as vended logs.
question: When could Application Load Balancer logs first go to CloudWatch Logs, and is it examinable?

values.display: Application Load Balancer (ALB) logs as vended logs

evidence.quote: Amazon CloudWatch Logs now supports Application Load Balancer (ALB) logs as vended logs, improving observability and simplifying debugging for network traffic patterns.

You can configure delivery of Application Load Balancer access logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon Data Firehose, and Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) with support for Apache Parquet format.

evidence.heading: Amazon CloudWatch Logs now supports Application Load Balancer logs

note: d129. Not examinable yet (after the 2026-07-15 cutoff). Current page: docs/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-logs.
